The Arabana, also known as the Ngarabana, are an Aboriginal Australian people of northern South Australia, on the west and southwest side of Kati Thanda, Lake Eyre.

Their country is dry, but it holds the mound springs, where water from the Great Artesian Basin rises to the surface. These springs were camping places and the route of travel and trade across the desert. Neighbours included the Dhirari across the lake, the Wangkangurru to the north and the Kokatha to the south.

The same line of springs later guided the Overland Telegraph of 1872 and the railway to Oodnadatta. In 2012 the courts recognised Arabana native title over a large area including part of the lake.
sum: The Arabana, also known as the Ngarabana, are an Aboriginal Australian people of northern South Australia, on the west and southwest side of Kati Thanda, Lake Eyre.
